claims.text: Online social networking is adversely associated with self-reported mental problems among Korean students.
Online social networking is adversely associated with suicidal thought among Korean students.

evidence.description: Hierarchical linear models analyzing Wave 4 and Wave 5 of the Korean Youth Panel Survey show an adverse association between online social networking and self-reported mental problems while controlling for time-lagged variables.

Hierarchical linear models analyzing Wave 4 and Wave 5 of the Korean Youth Panel Survey show an adverse association between online social networking and suicidal thought while controlling for time-lagged variables.

methodologies.name: Hierarchical Linear Modeling on Longitudinal Panel Data
methodologies.description: Hierarchical linear models were estimated on longitudinal panel data to probe the psychological effects of time spent online while holding constant time-lagged control variables at student and school levels.

limitations.text: The bulk of previous research on the pros and cons of online social media use is based on cross-sectional data, thereby precluding causal inference.
